::: {.page-about name="Reference page with practice" uses="a rule or code to look up (numerals, symbols, a key); examples, then a few to try" pieces="panel, blank"}
:::

{{< vocab "Roman numerals" zh=true >}} use seven letters from the Latin alphabet. You still see them on clocks, in book chapters and at the end of movies.

| Letter | I | V | X | L | C | D | M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Value** | 1 | 5 | 10 | 50 | 100 | 500 | 1000 |

::: side-by-side
::: {.panel title="Rule 1 · Bigger to smaller: add"}
**VI** = 5 + 1 = 6
**XV** = 10 + 5 = 15
**CLX** = 100 + 50 + 10 = 160
:::
::: {.panel title="Rule 2 · Smaller before bigger: subtract"}
**IV** = 5 − 1 = 4
**IX** = 10 − 1 = 9
**XL** = 50 − 10 = 40 · **XC** = 100 − 10 = 90
:::
:::

Never use the same letter more than three times in a row: 4 is **IV**, not ~~IIII~~.

## Try it

::: side-by-side
::: {}
**Roman → number**

**XII** = {{< blank 2.5cm answer="12" >}}

**XIX** = {{< blank 2.5cm answer="19" >}}

**LXV** = {{< blank 2.5cm answer="65" >}}

**MMXXVI** = {{< blank 2.5cm answer="2026" >}}

::: {}
**Number → Roman**

**8** = {{< blank 3cm answer="VIII" >}}

**24** = {{< blank 3cm answer="XXIV" >}}

**49** = {{< blank 3cm answer="XLIX" >}}

**this year** = {{< blank 3cm answer="MMXXVI" >}}
:::
